text:
alex: FYI - EU GPU pool saturated ~08:42 UTC, several routes backed up and we saw increased 504s.
jamal: saw it too. metrics spike on p50->p99 token latency, queue length jumped on the shared queue.
priya: any obvious cause? sudden tenant surge or model rollout?
alex: looks like a mix - a big batch job from partner-x + a canary of the new 16k context model on default route. head-of-line blocking on the single FIFO queue made it worse.
maria: ouch. that's the scenario we've feared for mixed-cost workloads.
sre-bot: Incident created INC-2026-234: EU GPU saturation. Paging oncall.
dmitri: current config is single global FIFO with per-tenant rate limits. no per-route isolation.
jamal: recommendation: try hybrid queues -> small high-priority per-route queues for low-latency routes + shared background queue for batch/cheap routes. also add token-bucket shaping per-GPU pool.
priya: agree. also consider soft admission that routes to CPU-quantized variant when queue depth exceeds threshold.
alex: quick config sketch I prototyped (very rough):

```yaml
admission:
  pools:
    eu-gpu:
      max_inflight: 200
      token_bucket:
        rate: 50/s
        burst: 100
  queues:
    - name: route-critical
      type: per-route
      priority: high
      max_inflight: 60
    - name: shared-background
      type: fifo
      priority: low
      max_inflight: 120
  fallback:
    on_queue_exhaustion: route-variant:cpu-quantized
``` 

jamal: + add feedback loop using queue length -> scale decision for dedicated capacity and route shedding thresholds. small hysteresis to avoid flapping.
maria: what about fairness? multi-tenant risk if we promote per-route queues for big customers.
dmitri: use weighted priority + aging so small/old requests don't starve: weight = base + age_factor.
priya: can we test this in canary? maybe enable on eu-west-1 pool with synthetic load and a real tenant A/B.
alex: plan: implement admission prototype, run 2h soak with traffic replay for canary routes, measure p50/p95/p99, token cost impact, and error rate. if + for latency and cost, roll to other regions.
ops-bot: link to replay job: https://internal.jobs/replay/17981
jamal: also track cost delta: switching to cpu-quantized fallback trades GPU tokens for longer latency but cheaper unit cost. need SLO guardrails.
maria: good point — add SLA-aware policy: never route low-tier traffic to cpu fallback if SLO flagged.
priya: one more idea: advertise per-route admission settings in the Console so product teams can signal latency criticalness.
alex: agreed. I'll open a PR with the prototype admission controller config and an e2e test harness. tagging @jamal @priya for review.
jamal: ack. I'll set up the canary cluster and replay harness.
dmitri: I'll mock the aging weights and fairness sim and run overnight.
sre-bot: Note: Created deployment window for canary 22:00-02:00 UTC to avoid peak hours.
alex: ta. let's sync tomorrow 09:30 UTC to review metrics from the canary.
maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
